GeeekPi Armor Lite V5 — Budget Beast with Retro Flair

★★★★½

The GeeekPi Armor Lite V5 punches way above its $16.99 price tag. This case combines a metal chassis with the Armor Lite V5 active cooler, which includes a 4010 PWM fan and copper heatsinks that keep your Pi 5's BCM2712 processor comfortably below 50°C under load.

What really sets it apart is the Game5Pi design heritage — it's built with retro gaming enthusiasts in mind. The case has a clean, compact profile that fits perfectly in a gaming setup or media center. It also supports PCIe peripheral boards (X1000/X1001/X1003/N04/N05), making it expandable for NVMe SSDs or other add-ons down the line.

For the price, you're getting active cooling and a metal case. That's almost unheard of at $17. The Armor Lite V5 cooler is whisper-quiet at idle and barely noticeable under full load.

Compatibility note: This case works with Raspberry Pi 5 4GB, 8GB, and even the newer 16GB variant — future-proofing you for the latest Pi 5 SKUs.

Argon ONE V3 — The Premium Standard

★★★★★

The Argon ONE V3 is the case that redefined what a Pi 5 case could be. Full machined aluminum construction gives it a Mac-like feel that's both sturdy and elegant. The aluminum body acts as a massive passive heatsink, and the 30mm PWM blower fan kicks in only when needed.

The killer feature? Full-size HDMI ports. The Pi 5 comes with micro HDMI, but the Argon ONE V3 reroutes them to full-size HDMI on the back panel — no more adapter dongles. It also includes a proper power button with safe shutdown functionality, something you don't realize you need until you have it.

The cable management is exceptional. All ports are rear-facing, which means your desk stays clean. The V3's black finish looks professional in any setting — home office, server rack, or entertainment center.

At $27 for the base model (or ~$54 for the M.2 NVMe version), it's twice the price of the GeeekPi, but you're paying for engineering polish that shows in every detail.

🏆 The Verdict: GeeekPi Armor Lite V5 Wins for Value

Here's the honest take: if budget is your primary concern, the GeeekPi Armor Lite V5 is the smarter buy. At $16.99, it includes active cooling, a metal chassis, PCIe expansion support, and works with all Pi 5 variants including the 16GB model. It's $10 cheaper than the Argon ONE V3 and still delivers excellent thermal performance.

But — and this is a real but — the Argon ONE V3 earns its premium price through polish. The full-size HDMI ports alone are a quality-of-life upgrade that makes daily use noticeably better. The aluminum body feels like a premium product, not an accessory. If you're building a Pi 5 desktop workstation or media center that sits on your desk every day, the Argon ONE V3 is worth the extra $10.

Our pick: GeeekPi Armor Lite V5. For most Pi 5 owners — especially retro gaming enthusiasts, hobbyists, and budget-conscious builders — it delivers 90% of the experience at 60% of the price. That's hard to beat.

Which Pi 5 Case Should You Buy?

Choose the GeeekPi Armor Lite V5 if:

  • You're on a budget and want the best bang for your buck
  • You're building a retro gaming console (RetroPie, Batocera)
  • You want PCIe expansion without breaking the bank
  • You have a Pi 5 16GB variant

Choose the Argon ONE V3 if:

  • Build quality and aesthetics matter most
  • You hate micro HDMI dongles and want full-size ports
  • A power button with safe shutdown is important to you
  • You're building a home server or desktop Pi 5 setup

Either way, you're getting a great case for the Raspberry Pi 5. The Pi 5 generates noticeably more heat than the Pi 4, so don't run it without a case — both of these options will keep your board cool and safe.
